result.title: EvoProbe: Evaluation-Driven Benchmark Evolution for LLM Agents
result.summary: Static benchmarks for large language model (LLM) agents face saturation and data contamination risks, motivating continual updates to evaluation tasks. However, aggregate scores and success rates offer limited insight into specific problem-solving bottlenecks and provide limited guidance for subsequent task design. We propose EvoProbe, an evaluation-driven benchmark evolution framework that integrates task generation, diagnostic evaluation, and feedback-driven regeneration into a closed loop. It combines verifiable subtask outcome scoring with evidence-supported multi-judge trajectory evaluation and distills phase-level bottlenecks, success patterns, and failure patterns into diagnostic feedback for generating new executable tasks. Across two rounds of cybersecurity experiments, evaluations of eight models on 66 tasks reveal phase-level performance differences and common failure patterns beyond aggregate scores. In a cross-round comparison with the Examiner model set and solver configuration held fixed, all eight models achieve lower Outcome scores on the updated tasks, with relative decreases of 11.8\% in mean Outcome and 40.0\% in mean Pass\textasciicircum{}3. These results support using fine-grained diagnostics to guide iterative task updates and probe agents' current capabilities and limitations.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EvoProbe：一个由评估驱动的 benchmark 演化框架，把任务生成、可验证子任务评分与多评审轨迹诊断、反馈再生成连成闭环，并在网络安全任务上对八个模型做两轮实验，揭示聚合分数之外的阶段级瓶颈与失败模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按阶段诊断轨迹瓶颈、归纳成功与失败模式的做法，可能为 LVR 推理轨迹的分阶段评价（如定位 THINK/LOOK/STOP 各阶段收益与失败）提供评价思路或线索；但对象是纯文本 LLM agent、无视觉与 latent 状态，可迁移性需人工核查。
